food.name: Cannellini Beans

identity.basisReason: Dry per-100g basis matches the stored staple ingredient and avoids dilution from soaking and cooking.
includes: dry white kidney beans sold as cannellini

scoreReadiness.summary: Every visible DBv2 metric is populated for the locked dry raw cannellini identity.
caveats: Dry beans must be soaked and fully cooked before eating; cooked values will be diluted by absorbed water.

sourceNotes: Production entry for plain dry raw cannellini beans on a per-100g basis.
USDA FoodData Central supplies the canonical dry-bean macros, starch, and minerals.
Exact cannellini research supplies the missing fat fractions, fibre, sugars, vitamins, and amino-acid pattern.
Required visible values are complete; no other bean's nutrient profile is used.

topPros.title: creamy texture works in proper meals
topPros.explanation: They blend into soups and sauces while still holding their shape in salads.

topPros.title: cheap dry pantry staple
topPros.explanation: A bag stores well and turns into several meals for very little money.

topPros.title: mild flavour takes seasoning well
topPros.explanation: Herbs, tomato, garlic, and stronger sauces all work.

topCons.title: they must be cooked properly
topCons.explanation: Raw or undercooked kidney beans can retain lectins, so this is not a casual low-heat ingredient.

topCons.title: can be rough on digestion
topCons.explanation: Like other beans, they can cause gas or bloating for some people.

topCons.title: dry beans take time and planning
topCons.explanation: Soaking and a full cook make them less convenient than opening a can.

explanation.summary: Proteins are carrying this food most, while vitamins are holding it back most. It lands in B tier.
